requirements.title: A procedure interface determines invocation reference forms
requirements.definition: The interface of a procedure determines the forms of reference through which it can be invoked.

pending.interface-determines-invocation-referenc: Define explicit interface for subroutine set_answer(x) and function answer(); use CALL for the subroutine and expression reference for the function, with sentinels -17 and expected values 42.

requirements.title: A procedure interface consists of name, binding label, generic identifiers, characteristics, and dummy names
requirements.definition: A procedure interface consists of its name, binding label, generic identifiers, characteristics, and dummy argument names.

pending.interface-name-component: Declare interface for external function answer and call answer() into sentinel -17; expect 42.
pending.interface-binding-label-component: Fortran-only positive plan: external subroutine s(n) BIND(C, NAME="cf_s") has INTEGER(C_INT), VALUE :: n and assigns module variable seen = n + 1; caller explicit interface repeats BIND(C, NAME="cf_s") and VALUE, initializes seen to -777, calls s(41_C_INT), and expects seen == 42, recording the binding label as an interface component.
pending.interface-generic-identifiers-component: Create generic interface gen binding function answer; call gen() into sentinel -777 and expect 42. Wrong-resolution sentinel companion also has a specific gen returning -999; removing the generic binding changes the result to -999, making generic resolution observable.
pending.interface-characteristics-component: Create generic interface with integer and real dummy specifics returning 41 and 42; real actual selects 42 from sentinel -777. Wrong-specific sentinel makes the integer specific return -999, so selection by the wrong characteristic is observable.
pending.interface-dummy-argument-names-component: Use explicit interface subroutine set_answer(value) and keyword CALL set_answer(value=actual) with actual initialized to -17; expect 42.

requirements.title: Procedure characteristics and binding label are fixed, while other interface components may vary by context
requirements.definition: A procedure's characteristics and binding label are fixed; the name, generic identifiers, and dummy argument names may differ in different contexts outside the stated separate-module exception.

pending.procedure-characteristics-fixed: Define a module function with integer dummy characteristic and call it through two interfaces that preserve that characteristic; actual 41 produces 42 in both calls.
pending.procedure-binding-label-fixed: Fortran-only positive plan: declare the external procedure and its explicit interface with the same BIND(C, NAME="cf_s") label and VALUE integer dummy; after seen is initialized to -777, CALL s(41_C_INT) sets seen to 42. A source-control mismatch companion is nonconforming, but no diagnostic facet is claimed for this unnumbered program requirement.
pending.procedure-names-generic-identifiers-dumm: Expose the same module function answer through generic identifiers gen1 and gen2; both calls initialize results to -777 and expect 42. Wrong-resolution sentinel companion binds gen2 to a different specific returning -999, so contextual generic identifier mapping is observable.

requirements.title: Separate module procedure bodies shall match dummy names and NON_RECURSIVE status from their interface body
requirements.definition: For a separate module procedure body, dummy argument names and NON_RECURSIVE attribute status are required to match the corresponding module procedure interface body.

pending.separate-module-body-dummy-names-match-i: Positive source-control declares a module procedure interface subroutine set_answer(value) and matching separate body set_answer(value) assigning 42; mismatch companion is nonconforming with no diagnostic claimed here.
pending.separate-module-body-non-recursive-match: Positive source-control uses matching NON_RECURSIVE status between module procedure interface body and separate body returning 42; mismatch companion is nonconforming with no diagnostic claimed here.

requirements.title: An abstract interface is procedure characteristics plus dummy argument names
requirements.definition: An abstract interface is a set of procedure characteristics together with the dummy argument names.
